# E0345: value parameter of a type that can't be compared

Two types are one type when their value arguments are equal, so a value parameter is an integer or a `bool`, which compare exactly. Use an integer, scaled if you need fractions.

- Rule: [`generics.value-parameters`](../../reference/07-types.md#generics.value-parameters)
- Reported at: the value parameter's type.
- Tier: `meta`, checked in the `items` phase

## Example

This program makes the mistake:

```stilt E0345:1
type Scaled<k: f64> = { value: f64 }
```

This one is fixed:

```stilt
type Scaled<k: i64> = { value: f64 }
```

## What the compiler prints

`stilt check` on [`E0345_value_parameter_of_a_type_that_cant_be_compared.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0345_value_parameter_of_a_type_that_cant_be_compared.lt):

```text
── VALUE PARAMETER OF A TYPE THAT CAN'T BE COMPARED ── E0345_value_parameter_of_a_type_that_cant_be_compared.lt:1:16  [E0345]

A value parameter's type is an integer type or `bool`, whose values compare
exactly, so two types with equal arguments are one type, and `f64` isn't one:

  1 │ type Scaled<k: f64> = { value: f64 }
    │                ^^^

Two types are one type when their value arguments are equal, so a value
parameter is an integer or a `bool`, which compare exactly. Use an integer,
scaled if you need fractions.

To fix it, use `i64`, whose values compare exactly:

  1 │ type Scaled<k: i64> = { value: f64 }
    │                ~~~
```
